solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Affected by being clothed in the genuine dressed hide

indicators.note: something clothed is wrapped round, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: the + real, i.e. genuine
as in 'down with flu': affected by

explanation.surface: Someone affected by being dressed in the real thing: a hide that has been treated.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle is Disorderly: in down clues the definition gives the entry, while the wordplay builds THEREWITHAL, which must be rearranged into WHITLEATHER for the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitleather is white leather, a hide dressed with alum, so it is literally a dressed hide.

clue.text: Caper is, in the Catholic Church, a deformity

definitions.note: defines MISCREATION, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: in places the caper and its companion word inside the church

blocks.note: Rome stands for the Roman Catholic Church
an antic is a playful caper
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prank that, within the Church, counts as something monstrous.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle is Disorderly: in across clues the wordplay builds the grid entry, and the definition gives a word made of the same letters, here MISCREATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreation is a misshapen or monstrous creation, which is what a deformity is.

clue.text: Rule introduced into US state to stay

indicators.note: introduced into means put inside the state's name

blocks.note: the north-eastern US state
R abbreviates rule, as in R for recipe-style rules

explanation.surface: A regulation brought into an American state allowing someone to stay on.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds MARINE; as a down entry it is rearranged into REMAIN, which the definition gives.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to stay where one is, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Related to old queen, chap surrenders his heart to song

indicators.note: surrendering the central letter to something means swapping that letter out for it

blocks.note: a chap is a man
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: A tale of a man who gives his heart to a song about a former queen.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue is normal: the wordplay gives the entry itself, with the A at the middle of MAN replaced by ARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Marian means relating to Mary, as in Queen Mary I of England, whose reign is the Marian period.

clue.text: Measures of land, seemingly limitless expanse, right?

blocks.note: the sea looks as though it goes on for ever
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Surveying land that seems to stretch without end: is that right?
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds SEAR; the down entry is its rearrangement ARES, which the definition gives.
explanation.definitionFit: An are is a metric unit of area, a hundred square metres, used for land.

clue.text: Hanky, rank, stuffed into mouth (7, two words)

indicators.note: something stuffed into another thing ends up inside it

blocks.note: os is the Latin for mouth, used in anatomy
a range is a row or rank

explanation.surface: A smelly handkerchief crammed into someone's mouth as a gag.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds ORANGES; the down entry is its rearrangement NOSE RAG, which the definition gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Nose rag is a slang name for a handkerchief, the cloth you blow your nose on.

clue.text: Fine discernment, special, as introduction to gallery

indicators.note: an introduction comes first, so the first piece leads off before the gallery

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for special
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: Refined judgement, something special, on show as you enter an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds STATE; the down entry is its rearrangement TASTE, which the definition gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is the ability to judge quality finely, especially in art and style.

clue.text: One supervising terminal crossing, an endless task

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a chore is a routine task

explanation.surface: Supervising a final crossing is a task that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds ANCHOR; the down entry is its rearrangement CHARON, a proper noun the preamble allows.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Charon ferries the dead across the Styx, the last crossing anyone makes.

clue.text: Puritan judgement, right to supplant Charles's head

indicators.note: to supplant is to take the place of, here of the first letter of Charles

blocks.note: a decision is a judgement
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A Puritan's verdict: the right man to replace King Charles's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds DERISION; the down entry is its rearrangement IRONSIDE. The surface recalls the execution of Charles I by the Puritans.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironsides were Cromwell's Puritan cavalry, and an Ironside is one of those Puritan soldiers.

clue.text: Union to make vigorous attack on leader of Socialists

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to go at is to attack vigorously
the opening letter of Socialists

explanation.surface: A trade union preparing to lay into the head of the Socialists.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds GOATS; the down entry is its rearrangement SOGAT, the Society of Graphical and Allied Trades, a former British printing union.
explanation.definitionFit: SOGAT was a British trade union for print workers, so it is a union by name.

clue.text: Seam-like join: it covers gap in the partition

definitions.note: defines RAPHE, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: the letters run across the space between two words, covering that gap

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A seam-like joint bridging a gap in a dividing wall.
explanation.walkthrough: As an across clue, the wordplay gives the entry HEPAR (liver of sulphur); the definition gives RAPHE, made of the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A raphe is an anatomical seam-like ridge where two halves of a structure have joined.

clue.text: Old poet's probably left Romania — article written about it

definitions.note: defines OTHER, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: written about means set around, so the country sits inside

blocks.note: the definite article
RO is Romania's international code

explanation.surface: A poet of old has likely quit Romania, and a piece is written about it.
explanation.walkthrough: As an across clue, the wordplay gives the entry THROE; the definition points to OTHER, the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In old poetic usage other could mean the remaining or left one, and 'probably' hedges that archaic sense.

clue.text: Wretched lament following fresh increase in size

indicators.note: something wretched is in a sorry, broken state, so its letters are muddled
following places the second piece after the first

blocks.note: green means fresh or new
the letters of lament rearranged

explanation.surface: A miserable complaint after a fresh growth spurt.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds GREENMANTLE, John Buchan's novel and one of the preamble's proper nouns; the down entry is its rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An enlargement is the act or result of making something bigger.

clue.text: The writer's in a hurry, not quite finishing propositions

definitions.note: defines PREMISES, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: falling just short of the end means the final letter is lost

blocks.note: the writer is I, so the writer's is I'm

explanation.surface: An author in a rush, leaving arguments unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: As an across clue, the wordplay gives the entry IMPRESSE, an old word for an emblem; the definition gives PREMISES, the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Premises are the propositions an argument starts from.

clue.text: An error — take off part of crust

definitions.note: defines SIMA, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: the instruction to take off is literal: remove those very letters

blocks.note: the article
an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A slip in baking: remove some of the pastry crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' is a self-referential instruction: delete the letters TAKE. The entry AMIS is a proper noun (the novelists) and an anagram of SIMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sima is the lower layer of the Earth's crust, rich in silica and magnesium.

clue.text: Wild tree, new one, left plant community different from its neighbour

definitions.text: plant community different from its neighbour
definitions.note: defines ALTERNE, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: something wild is unruly, so its letters run free

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a means one
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A wild tree, a new one, left in a patch of vegetation unlike the one next to it.
explanation.walkthrough: As an across clue, the wordplay gives the entry ETERNAL; the definition gives ALTERNE, made of the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alterne is an ecological term for a plant community that alternates with, and differs from, an adjacent one.

clue.text: Bit of reggae in rock period tracks

definitions.note: defines RAILS, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: a bit of the word is just its first letter here
in sets one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the Lias is a series of Lower Jurassic rocks and its period
the opening letter of reggae

explanation.surface: A snatch of reggae among the rock tracks of a particular era.
explanation.walkthrough: As an across clue, the wordplay gives LIRAS, plural of the Italian currency; the definition gives RAILS, the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rails are the tracks a train runs on.

clue.text: Gives fresh look to senior crumbling in part

indicators.note: crumbling masonry falls apart, so the letters break up and resettle
in places the broken-up word within the short form

blocks.note: PT is the abbreviation for part
the letters of senior rearranged

explanation.surface: Refreshing the look of an old building whose senior parts are crumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds PERONIST, a follower of Juan Perón; the down entry is its rearrangement REPOINTS, which the definition gives.
explanation.definitionFit: To repoint brickwork is to renew its mortar joints, which smartens the wall's appearance.

clue.text: Company sat after changing outdoor wear?

definitions.note: defines COATS, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: changing alters the order of the letters
after puts the shuffled piece behind the company

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
the letters of sat rearranged

explanation.surface: A group sitting down after putting on their outdoor clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: As an across clue, the wordplay gives COSTA, a rib; the definition gives COATS. The question mark admits that coats are only one kind of outdoor wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Coats are worn outdoors over other clothes, an example of outdoor wear.

clue.text: Small horses docked inside vehicle — local anaesthetic required

definitions.note: defines PROCAINE, the anagram of the entry

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the final letter goes
inside places the shortened animals within the vehicle

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
ponies are small horses

explanation.surface: Ponies with docked tails in a trailer need a local anaesthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: As an across clue, the wordplay gives CAPONIER, a covered passage in a fortification; the definition gives PROCAINE, the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Procaine is a drug used to numb a small area, a local anaesthetic.

clue.text: To be effective at a specific time, playwright must pen one

definitions.text: To be effective at a specific time

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it, as in a sheep pen

blocks.note: Harold Pinter, the English dramatist
a means one

explanation.surface: To work in time, a dramatist has to write one piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds PAINTER; the down entry is its rearrangement PERTAIN. The definition is loose, as the blogger and a commenter noted: pertain usually means to belong or apply.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertain means to apply or be relevant, so loosely to be in force at a given time.

clue.text: One making forecast by means of German

definitions.note: defines PRESAGER, the anagram of the entry

blocks.note: as per: according to, by way of
GER is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A forecaster working in German.
explanation.walkthrough: As an across clue, the wordplay gives ASPERGER, a sprinkler of holy water; the definition gives PRESAGER, the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A presager is one who presages, foretelling what is to come.

clue.text: It's grand to guide returning birds

indicators.note: returning goes back the way it came, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
to steer is to guide

explanation.surface: Great fun to lead the birds back home as they return.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds GREETS; the down entry is its rearrangement EGRETS, which the definition gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are white herons, a kind of wading bird.

clue.text: I'll occupy position on an impressive scale

blocks.note: a place is a position

explanation.definitionFit: Epical means epic in quality, grand and heroic in scale.

clue.text: Reside on fringes of Nailstone, Leicestershire village

blocks.note: to stay is to reside
the first and last letters of Nailstone

explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds STANEY; the down entry is its rearrangement ANSTEY, a proper noun. Nailstone is itself a real Leicestershire village, which makes the surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: Anstey is a village just north-west of Leicester, in the English county of Leicestershire.

clue.text: Caves, kind giving good accommodation? Reverse of that

explanation.walkthrough: As an across clue, the wordplay gives TROGS (louts); the definition gives GROTS, poetic caves, the same letters.

clue.text: Plant fibre I fed to dam?

indicators.note: food fed to an animal goes inside it

blocks.note: a dam is a mother animal; a mare is one example, hence the question mark
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Ramie is a strong fibre from an Asian nettle-like plant, used for textiles.

clue.text: Distinguished Japanese statesman, feature of bygone regimes

clue.text: Something for Burns Night writer included in bits of Scots elegy

clue.text: Bury, no longer warm and dry, in the north, stormy

definitions.note: defines INEARTH, the anagram of the entry

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: Ditch near Aviemore winter sportsman almost flipped over
